issues.detail: The Greek 'ασπαζεται υμας' (aspazate hymas) is an imperative meaning 'Greet/Embrace one another'. The Vietnamese translation 'Chào anh em' (Greet brothers) misses the reflexive/reciprocal sense of the Greek, which implies a mutual greeting among the recipients.

The Greek 'πεπληρωμενοι' (peplērōmenoi) is a perfect passive participle meaning 'having been filled'. The Vietnamese 'đầy đủ' (complete/sufficient) captures the state but misses the specific nuance of being 'filled' by the Spirit/God.
